Zhuangzi said:
"The five colors disorder the eyes, causing the eyes to lose their clarity."
The five sounds confuse the ears, causing them to lose their acuity;
the five odors confuse the nose, thereby impairing its sense of smell;
the five flavors clog the mouth, making it harsh and unpleasant.
Grasping and rejecting causes the mind to become slippery and the nature to fly away; these five give rise to harm, which harms the five faculties.
This is largely the same as what is said regarding old age.
Although that teaching speaks of harming living beings, it does not know the root of harming living beings.
Knowing only that they are harmed by the five [aggregates], they are forever deluded regarding the method for removing those harms.

The character *quán* (悛) is pronounced with the *qián* rhyme; the character *zhòu* (噣) is pronounced with the *jiù* rhyme, meaning "beak. The character *huì* (喙) is pronounced with the *huì* rhyme, also meaning "mouth. One should know that in the teachings of the Elder [Confucius], there was never a time when form did not exist, nor has there ever been one who was not blind.
This may be analogously applied even to the mind of smoothness (*ślakṣṇa*).

Regarding the statement in the "Contemplation of the Provisional" (*prajñapti-darśana*) that one is still said to "enter the emptiness of form," this is a refutation of the preceding contemplation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-darśana*).
If one cannot comprehend all Buddha-dharmas within form,
but merely names it the "emptiness of form" and grasps at it through acceptance,
this is what can be seen in the Madhyamaka.
Therefore, the *Śāstra* states that the following section is a further censure of the Lesser Vehicle.
Thus, we know that the two vehicles do not perceive the reality of form.
The subsequent passage provides a profound critique, which expresses the intent of the critique based on principle.
Within the practice of the phenomenal realm, one must reprove desire while simultaneously incorporating the perfect principle;
only then can it be considered the skillful means of the Perfect Teaching.
Therefore, it is said that the intent lies herein.
People do not see that this is for the purpose of literary composition.
May you deign to convey this intent to those above and below.
*Zhi guan fu xing chuan hong jue*, Scroll Four, Part Three.
